findings.title: Deposit is within the amount cap
findings.detail: This amount check does not verify deposit protection or authenticity. Annual rent GBP 15600; cap = 15600 / 52 * 5 (GBP 1500.00 rounded down to pennies); requested GBP 1500. Importance: 85/100. Conditional: Confirm that the rented property is in England. Confirm this is an ordinary private tenancy, not an excluded arrangement. Confirm that rent and deposit cover the same whole tenancy. The amount calculation holds on the quoted figures: GBP 1300 x 12 = GBP 15,600 a year, and 15,600 / 52 x 5 = GBP 1,500. The GBP 1,500 deposit in s6 is therefore at the cap, not above it, so there is no excess-deposit concern. No counter-evidence defeats this calculation, and I have not changed it. However, the cap only applies if the tenancy is a covered one. Jurisdiction and tenancy type are "unknown", and nothing in the contract confirms the property is in England (s2 gives only a London postcode, which is not a conclusion). The contract also does not say the rent and deposit cover the same whole tenancy. These facts are unresolved, so the issue stays conditional rather than being upheld or dismissed. This amount check says nothing about deposit protection or authenticity. Sources: https://www.gov.uk/guidance/tenant-fees-act-2019-guidance-for-tenants
